newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to process 14.5 mln tonnes of crude in '96.
newsitem.headline: Romania to process 14.5 mln tonnes of crude in '96.

text.p: Romania processed 8.7 million tonnes of crude oil over January-August and plans to process a total 14.5 tonnes (roughly 290,000 barrels per day) by the end of 1996, a senior industry ministry official said on Tuesday.
That compares with output in 1995 of 15.2 million tonnes (305,000 bpd) processed by Romania's 12 underused refineries, which have a total capacity of 34 million tonnes (680,000 bpd).
"Our plan is to process 14.5 million tonnes of crude this year," said Mircea Turtureanu, general director in charge of the ministry's chemical and petrochemical department.

Turtureanu said Romania would import 2.4 million tonnes of crude over the next three months. Domestic production for the rest of the year would total 1.5 million tonnes. Romania pumps some 6.6 million tonnes (132,000 bpd) of crude each year.
Figures for September crude imports were not yet available, a ministry official said.
Turtureanu said up to 68 percent of costs for crude imports by would be covered by export earnings from processed products.
Romania must import large quantities of crude for domestic energy needs and to keep its refineries operating at a minimum.
Last winter, an acute shortage of convertible currency sharply cut crude imports and the state Renel RA electricity authority cut power supplies to industry in January-March.

Last week, Bucharest guaranteed a $200 million loan for crude imports by the state Romanian Oil Company (CRP) over the next few months to preclude a fresh crisis. The loan was arranged with Chase Manhattan.

On Monday, Renel said it would spend $160 million to import fuel oil for its power plants for the coming winter months. Western oil dealers confirmed Renel would buy around 500,000 tonnes of high sulphur fuel oil over the next month.
Turtureanu also said the government was considering plans to trim refining capacity to an annual 16-18 million tonnes (320,000-360,000 bpd) over the next three years.

He said the newly-created CRP, a holding covering 12 state- owned refineries, four transport and 41 oil distribution companies as well as an oil exploration company, was expected to play a major role in streamlining the oil sector, now beset by bad management and inefficiency.
The official view is that the CRP would provide funds to import crude oil as well as streamline exploration, refining, distribution and transport of oil.
Some Western analysts said CRP was an old-style bureaucratic conglomerate and a step backward for reforms in the oil industry which could discourage foreign investors.
